title: Episode 1: Arrival
text:
Martin: I spy with my little eye something beginning with ... C.
Kara: Cars.
Mum: What?
Kara: There are lots of cars. Where are they all going?
Mum: It's getting dark.
Martin: Is it far?
Kara: Mum? Why can't we go on a real holiday?
Mum: This is a real holiday. You'll love it.
Martin: How much further? How. Much. Furtherrrrr?
Kara: Be quiet, Martin.
Mum: What's that, Kara?
Kara: Nothing. So, where are we going? We've been driving since this morning.
Mum: I told you, it's a secret.
Martin: Yeah, it's a secret, Kara.
Kara: I know.
Martin: Are we there? I'm hungry.
Kara: We're lost, aren't we?
Mum: Not very lost. I just need to find where we are on the map.
Kara: Why don't you use your phone?
Mum: Ah, good idea. What would I do without you, Kara? Oh. There's no signal.
Kara: I don't believe it!
Mum: Let's go on. I'm sure we'll find a road sign or a house ... or a phone box.
Kara: What's wrong?
Mum: It's a crossroads. Which way do we go? Uh, there must be a sign.
Kara: Maybe it fell over. I'll look.
Kara: Ahhh! Ahhh!
Mum: KARA!
Martin: What's happening?!
Howard: Max! MAX! Steady on boy, now calm DOWN!
Kara: Mum?
Mum: It's OK. It's just a dog.
Howard: Open the window!
Howard: Don't worry – the dog won't hurt you. Max loves people.
Martin: Yeah, right. He's got a strange way of showing it.
Howard: Are you lost?
Mum: Yes, we are. We're looking for –
Howard: Owl Hall?
Mum: That's right. How did you know?
Howard: It's the only place around here ... Apart from my house, of course. I'm Howard, by the way.
Mum: Hello, Howard. Nice to meet you.

Howard: There was a sign here once. But it fell down in the storms last year. Go straight ahead and after 800 metres you'll see a turning to the left. Go down the road and you'll come to Owl Hall. Enjoy your stay.
Mum: Thanks!
Mum: Can you see anything? Wait a minute. There it is!
Martin: Where are we?
Mum: We're here. Owl Hall.
Mum: Please can you open the gate for me, darling?
Kara: Why me? OK.
Kara: Brrr ... it's freezing.
Kara: OK!
Ghostly voice: Kara. Help me. Let me go!
Kara: What was that? Hello? Is someone there? Hello?

title: Episode 2: Exploring
text:
Martin: Creepy.
Kara: What?
Martin: This place. Owl Hall. It's creepy.
Kara: I know.
Mum: So? What do you think?
Kara: Err ... Wow.
Mum: They told me the keys were under the owl on the left.
Martin: Cool. It's a little stone owl. You can hide things there. I'm going to hide your phone there, Kara ...
Kara: Shhh.
Mum: Look! Here's a plan of the house. Hmmm. This must be the kitchen.
Mum: What an amazing kitchen!
Kara: Where are we, Mum?
Mum: Owl Hall. I told you. Isn't it great?
Martin: Kara, I'm bored. Can we go and explore the house?
Kara: Can we explore, Mum?
Mum: I can't but you can. I'll need to make us something to eat. Don't go too far. And don't go outside. It's too late.
Kara & Martin: Yes!
Martin: This is my room! You can have the other one.
Kara: It's like a prison cell.
Martin: I know. That's why I like it.
Kara: Don't talk rubbish, Martin. I can't believe it! We're cut off from the world.
Martin: What do you want a phone for anyway? You haven't got any friends. I think I saw a laptop in your room. Maybe you can use the internet.
Kara: Really?
Kara: OK. Here we go ... Welcome to Owl Hall. Click here to start.
Kara: That's weird. I can't close the page ...
Martin: Spooky! We're in prison at Owl Hall.
Kara: Please choose from the following options: Explore Owl Hall – Blog – About Owl Hall.
Kara: OK. I want to know where we are. So ... About Owl Hall.
Kara: Hmm ... there's no map. Well, I can't find out where we are but I can write a blog.
Mum: Dinner's ready!
Kara: Coming!
Kara: What are you doing, Martin?
Martin: Kara, can I talk to you?
Kara: Of course you can, Martin. What do you want to talk about?
Martin: Something's not right. I ... don't know how to say it.
Kara: It's okay, Martin. I'm listening.
Martin: It's this place ... this holiday. I've got a bad feeling, Kara. Please don't laugh at me.
Kara: I'm not laughing.
Martin: I think someone is watching us.
Martin: No. I think I saw someone in the courtyard. It was while you were using the computer. You won't let them take me away, will you, Kara? Please, promise you won't leave me.
Kara: I won't leave you.

title: Episode 3: Feeling Awkward
text:
Mum: Why was your bedroom door shut earlier?
Kara: I'm allowed some privacy, aren't I, Mum?
Mum: Of course you are. But –
Kara: But what? Are you worried I'm going to do something stupid again?
Mum: No, of course not.
Martin: Kara! There's no TV!
Kara: Mum? Is there really no TV?
Mum: I wanted to find somewhere quiet to go on holiday. Somewhere we could spend some time together.
Mum: Where are you going?
Kara: I'm not hungry anymore.
Kara: Martin?
Martin: I'm in here. In the living room.
Kara: What are you doing, Martin?
Martin: Look Kara! I'm making a fire. Come and help me!
Kara: I don't think we should make a fire Martin. Mum will be very angry.
Martin: Are you ready Kara?
Kara: Martin! Don't!
Mum: Kara – what's going on?!
Martin: She started it!
Kara: It was Martin!
Mum: You're tired Kara. Go to bed.
Kara: But Mum –
Mum: I said – go to bed!
Kara: OK, let's try writing a blog.
Kara: Welcome to your personal blog. Day 1. Fine. But what do I write? 'Hi!'
Kara: This is stupid. OK.
Kara: 'My name is Kara and this is my blog. We arrived here today. We = me, my mum, and my brother Martin.'
Mum: Good morning Kara! Sleep well? It's a lovely day. What do you want for breakfast? Toast … cereal ... how about ...
Kara: I'm not hungry. Can I go out?
Mum: Alright but don't go too far.
Kara: Thanks.
Kara: Martin?! I'm going to explore outside.
Martin: I can't hear you!
Kara: I said I'm going outside!
Martin: OK. I'll be there in a minute.
Kara: Still no signal. Wait a minute. I can use the phone to make a video. Let's see ... Awkward Productions presents ... Owl Hall – the movie ... directed by Kara. ... Here we are at the back of the house ... there are a lot of bushes and trees ... And over to the right, there's a ... what is it? It must be a barn. ... What's ... what's that? Hello? Who's there?
Martin: Ah HA!!!
Kara: Martin! The phone! My video! What's your PROBLEM?
Martin: Calm down! What is it Kara? What's wrong? Why do you look so frightened? Have you seen a ghost?
Kara: Shhhhhh.

title: Episode 4: Spy Catching
text:
Kara: Martin?
Kara: Where are we going?!
Martin: I want to see where this track goes.
Kara: We're going too far from Owl Hall.
Martin: So what? Come on!
Kara: I think we should go back.
Martin: No, there's a house up that hill. I want to see it.
Kara: Martin! Be careful!
Martin: Max! It's OK. We're friends. He's OK. He's big but he won't hurt you.
Kara: Look at the house.
Martin: Seriously spooky.
Kara: This must be Howard's house. He said he had a house near Owl Hall. Look! There's a face at one of the windows!
Martin: Come on! Let's get out of here!
Martin: What are you doing?
Kara: I was making a video, remember? Before you jumped on me?
Martin: I said I was sorry!
Kara: Well, if I connect my phone to the laptop we can play it back.
Kara: OK ... here we go.
Martin: Awkward Productions? You are seriously crazy.
Kara: Wait ... it comes later ... This is it! Look, Martin. Can you see? There's someone watching us!
Martin: It's a spy.
Kara: I'm going to upload the video to my blog.
Kara: What's that? 'You have 1 new message. Click here to read.'
Martin: Go on!
Martin: What does it say?
Kara: "I need to talk to you. Meet me in the barn at five o'clock. Come alone. A friend."
Martin: It's a message from the spy. Be careful. It might be a trap.
Kara: Don't be stupid.
Martin: What's that?
Kara: It's the door. Someone's here.
Kara: I'll go. Don't read my blog, Martin!
Martin: Why would I want to read your blog?
Howard: Hello. I'm Howard. Do you remember me?
Kara: I remember.
Howard: Is your mother at home?
Kara: I think so.
Kara: Mum! We've got a visitor. M-u-m?!
Mum: Howard! What are you doing here?'
Howard: I wanted see how you are.
Mum: Oh we're fine. I was just getting some exercise. Kara, darling ... Please can you go and make some tea? Would you like some tea, Howard?
Howard: I'd love some.
Mum: Kara?
Kara: Kara, darling ... Please can you go and make some tea, darling? And leave us alone, darling? … Alone. Come alone. I need to talk to you. Meet me in the barn at five o'clock. A friend.

title: Episode 5: The Bedroom
text:
Martin: Come on, Kara. It's time to go and meet the spy!
Kara: You can't come with me. He said I had to go alone.
Martin: He? How do you know the spy is a he? Anyway, I'm not going to let you go on your own. I'm coming and that's final. What are you looking at?
Kara: The picture on the wall.
Martin: It's the same picture you have in your room at home.
Kara: Exactly. 'The Bedroom' by Vincent van Gogh. It's my favourite painting. Don't you think that's strange? To find the same picture here?
Martin: Not really. Vincent van Gogh was mad too. He cut off his ear. Ouch!
Kara: Stop playing around. Let's go to the barn.
Martin: Wow. Look at all this stuff!
Kara: I thought it would be empty.
Martin: Furniture, paintings, boxes, computers ... This place is amazing!
Kara: What time is it?
Martin: Ten past five. The spy is late.
Kara: Hello? Is anyone here?
Martin: Come on. Let's go back.
Kara: Wait. I think I heard something.
Martin: It's your imagination. I'm bored. I'm going to play darts. Coming?
Kara: I'm coming ... in a minute. ... Hello? Are you here?
Kara: Mum?
Mum: Kara. I'm just making dinner.
Kara: Are there other people staying here? I mean, in the other buildings?
Mum: I don't know. I don't think so. Howard didn't say anything.
Kara: Howard? Why would he know?
Mum: He lives up the road. So, he knows who comes and who goes.
Kara: Have you met him before?
Mum: Howard? No, of course not. Why?
Kara: No reason. I was just curious. ... How long until dinner, Mum?
Mum: Five minutes.
Kara: OK. I'll be back in a minute.
Martin: And Martin is throwing his final dart to win. And it's a ... nineteen ...
Kara: Hey, Martin.
Martin: This is cool. Do you want to play?
Kara: Not really.
Martin: Your loss. I've been thinking. About the spy. I think I need to teach him something.
Kara: Teach him? What do you mean?
Martin: I want to teach him that it's bad to spy on other people.
Martin: After dinner I'm going to go spy hunting. Do you want to come?
Kara: No, I don't. You won't hurt him, will you?
Martin: Bullseye!!
Kara: Please be careful. Martin is looking for you. Send. I hope it's not too late.
Kara: 'Thanks for the warning.' Who are you? Why didn't you come to the barn? Send. Come on. Answer. Please.
Kara: 'I'm a friend. I went to the barn but you weren't alone. I heard you talking to someone. How about tomorrow morning, at eight o'clock?' I'll be there. Send. Don't let Martin catch you. Please. Please.

title: Episode 6: Something Bad
text:
Kara: Hello? Are you there? Hello?
Boy: Hello. Are you alone?
Kara: Yes, I am. Where are you?
Boy: Over here! Welcome to my home.
Kara: Your home? Do you live here alone in the barn?
Boy: Not really. I'm staying in the smallest cottage. But I like it here. People don't come here.
Kara: Don't you like people? What's your name? ... Okaay. My name's –
Boy: Kara. I know. It's a nice name.
Kara: In your message, you said that you needed to talk to me. Why?
Boy: Do you remember that you heard a voice ... when you arrived at Owl Hall?
Kara: Yes, I remember. Was it your voice?
Boy: No. What did the voice say?
Kara: I ...
Martin: Don't tell him, Kara.
Kara: What are you doing here?
Martin: What do you want? Leave Kara alone.
Boy: What's wrong? Is it your brother? Tell him to go and leave us alone.
Martin: I'm not going anywhere. I think you should go.
Kara: Martin's right. You should go.
Boy: Fine, then. If that's what you want.
Martin: Did you see that? I made him go! He was scared of me! Kara! Hey! Where are you going? Kara! Kaara! Where are you going?!
Mum: Are pancakes OK for breakfast?
Kara and Martin: Yes.
Martin: Shall we tell Mum ... about your friend, the spy?
Kara: He's not a spy.
Mum: Who's not a spy?
Kara: Why can't you leave me alone?!
Mum: Kara! Where are you going?
Martin: Where are you going?
Martin: Kara? Are you going to see your boyfriend? Last night you lied to me, Kara. Why did you do that?
Kara: I don't know what you mean.
Martin: Last night, when I came back you asked me if I'd found the spy. I told you he'd managed to escape, that someone must have warned him. And you said – 'It wasn't me'.
Kara: I didn't lie to you.
Martin: You're doing it again. Why are you lying to me?
Kara: I'm not lying to you!
Martin: And this morning ... you left me alone. You broke your promise.
Kara: What did I promise?
Martin: You promised not to leave me! Kara. Why are you looking at me like that?
Kara: Like what?
Martin: Like ... like you hate me. Like you want to kill me.
Kara: Martin ... Martin ... I'm sorry, Martin. I'm sorry, Martin. I promise I won't leave you. I promise I won't leave you.

title: Episode 7: A Noise in the Night
text:
Kara: What was that?
Kara: Martin?
Kara: Martin! Are you in there?
Kara: Martin! What have you done?!
Martin: I'm making a fire.
Kara: Where's Mum? Is she still inside the house? Please say she's not inside the house.
Kara: Martin!! Mum!!! No-o-o-o-o!!!
Mum: Kara! Kara! Are you alright?
Kara: I ... err ... I err ... I was ...
Mum: You were sleepwalking. Are you alright?
Kara: I'm alright. It was ... it was a dream.
Mum: Here. Have some hot chocolate.
Kara: Thanks, Mum.
Mum: Tell me about your dream.
Kara: I was in bed and ... I heard a noise ... I didn't know what it was so I went downstairs and I walked out into the courtyard. It was dark outside but there was a strange orange light in the sky. I started running ... as fast as I could ... past the cottage and down the path towards the barn. As I came closer, I could hear the noise getting louder and the light was getting brighter. And then I could see ... The barn was on fire! I tried to get inside but there was too much heat. Then I heard the sound of an alarm coming from the house. I ran back and ... Owl Hall was on fire. There were flames in all the windows ... And in the middle of the courtyard ...
Mum: Go on. I'm listening.
Kara: Martin was sitting on the ground ...
Mum: Martin?
Kara: He was watching the fire. I asked him where you were, Mum. I asked if you were still in the house ... and he looked at me with horror in his eyes. He got up and he ran into the building. Then I saw him at one of the upstairs windows ... he was holding out his hand to me. Then the roof collapsed and Martin disappeared and ... I woke up.
Mum: Kara. It's alright. ... I've asked Howard to come and see us tomorrow.
Kara: Oh no! He's spooky.
Mum: Howard is a friend so I want you to be nice to him. Is that OK?
Kara: OK.
Kara: Martin? Are you awake?
Martin: No.
Kara: I just had a terrible dream.
Martin: I know.
Kara: How do you know?
Martin: I was in it, remember? Why didn't you come into the house with me?
Kara: I ...
Martin: I held out my hand to you, but you didn't come!

title: Episode 8: Keep Out
text:
Kara: Hello? Hello? Oh! There you are.
Boy: Hello. Are you alone?
Kara: Yes, I am.
Boy: Where's your brother?
Kara: He's in his room. He wants to be alone. He put a Keep Out sign on the door.
Boy: Good.
Kara: He thinks you're a spy. Are you?
Boy: Maybe.
Kara: What are you writing?
Boy: This? Oh. Nothing. ... I know a place where your brother won't find us. Do you want to go there?
Kara: OK.
Boy: Come on!
Boy: Come on!
Kara: Where are we going?
Boy: You'll see. It's not far.
Boy: What's wrong?
Kara: I don't know you. I don't even know your name.
Boy: What's so important about a name? Would you trust me more if you knew it?
Kara: I ... don't know.
Boy: Come on!
Kara: OK!
Kara: Wow. A lake. Wow. It's amazing!
Boy: I know where there's a boat. Come on. I'll take you to the island.
Kara: An island?
Boy: Come on. ... Help me turn the boat over.
Boy: I'll row.
Kara: OK.
Kara: How did you find this place?
Boy: Last week when I was out walking I found the boat and rowed it here. Now I come here every day. It's my island.
Kara: You're strange!
Boy: You are too.
Boy: Do you ever feel like someone or something is chasing you?
Kara: No.
Boy: I do.
Kara: Why are they chasing you?
Boy: Because I'm different.
Kara: We're all different. Everyone in the world is different.
Boy: No, they're not. Everyone else is the same or trying to be the same. But you and me, we're different. That's why we're here.
Kara: On the island?
Boy: No, stupid. That's why we're at Owl Hall.

title: Episode 9: Missing Martin
text:
Kara: Today has been the best day of my life. I have a friend and his name is ... John! I'm so happy he finally told me his name just before we said goodbye. So, what else have I discovered about my new friend, apart from his name? He's an only child. He doesn't have any brothers or sisters. I can't imagine being an only child.
Mum: Kara!
Kara: OK. ... Martin?
Mum: Kara!
Kara: Martin?! Mum's calling. Are you there?
Kara: That's strange. Where are all Martin's things? Martin ... where ARE you?
Mum: Kara! Can you come down to the kitchen, please?
Kara: Coming! ... I was just ... oh.
Howard: Hello, Kara.
Mum: I told you Howard was coming. Remember?
Kara: Mum? Have you seen Martin?
Mum: Howard ...
Kara: What's happening?
Howard: Your mother says that you've been sleepwalking.
Kara: That's none of your business! You're not my dad!!
Mum: Kara, please don't talk to Howard like that. He's trying to help you.
Kara: If Howard wants to help me, then he can tell me where Martin is!
Mum: Please don't start! Not about Martin, please!
Howard: Please sit down, Kara. We have to talk. Martin is in a safe place. You don't have to worry about him. You have look after yourself now. Your mother and I are worried about you and we want to help you.
Kara: I promised not to leave him!
Mum: Please, Kara ... Please don't start talking about Martin again.
Kara: Where is he?
Howard: I told you. Martin is in a safe place.
Kara: No!
Kara: Martin? Where are you? What have you done?
Kara: A safe place ... a safe place ... of course ... the house on the hill .... Howard's house.

title: Episode 10: An Important Discovery
text:
Kara: Hello! Hello!
John: Come in. We can talk in my bedroom.
Kara: I need your help!
John: What are you talking about? What's happened?
Kara: I think Martin has been kidnapped. I think Howard has taken him and locked him in the basement of his house. I went there.
John: You went to the house on the hill?
Kara: I found a letter. It was addressed to Doctor Howard Ward. Howard's a doctor.
John: I know. Did you go into the basement?
Kara: You've got to come! I think Howard has taken him and locked him in the basement. There are people inside and I can't open the door and ... I promised I wouldn't leave him. Please help me.
John: OK, Kara. Let's go and find him.
Kara: What's that? On the wall?
John: It's a map of Treasure Island. It used to be my favourite book. I like islands. You know that.
Kara: And what's your favourite colour?
John: It's green. Why?
Kara: It's strange. The walls of your room are your favourite colour. The walls in my room in the main house are my favourite colour. You have a painting of your favourite book on the wall. I have my favourite painting on my wall. ... It's ... strange.
John: Come on! Let's go to the house on the hill.
John: Do you recognize the voices? Kara?
Kara: It's Mum! It's Mum's and Howard's voices. What are they doing in the basement?
John: There's a key ... somewhere ... here it is.
Kara: How did you know the key was there?
John: I'm a spy, remember? Are you sure you want to do this?
Kara: Yes! Unlock the door!
Howard: You have to be patient, Janet.
Mum: I can't be patient! It happened more than six months ago. I can't do this anymore!
Kara: What ... what is this place? Why are there so many television monitors?!
John: They're linked to cameras all around Owl Hall. Look. The entrance ... the courtyard ... And here ... the main house kitchen.
Kara: Shhh, listen.
Mum: You told me that everything would be alright!
Howard: It is alright. You heard what Kara said. She said that Martin had gone.
Mum: We have to find her.
Howard: Come with me. I know how we can find her.
John: We have to leave. I think they're coming here.
Kara: I don't understand. What's happening?
John: They won't find us here. There aren't any cameras in the barn.
Kara: But where's Martin? I thought he would be in the basement. I have to find him.
John: Kara, Martin's gone.
Kara: What do you mean?
John: I mean you don't have to worry about Martin anymore. You can live your own life now.
Kara: You don't know anything about my brother.
John: You're right. So tell me what happened. What really happened six months ago? Tell me and then maybe I'll understand him better. Go on. What are you waiting for, Kara?
Kara: OK. I'll tell you. But you must promise not to tell Mum or Howard.
John: I promise.

title: Episode 11: Kara's Story (Part 1)
text:
Kara: I don't know where to start ... But I suppose it was six months ago on that Saturday morning when Mum and Dad told us that they were going to separate.
Mum: Dad has to go to Australia as part of his new job.
Kara: We both knew the real reason he was going to Australia. We had both heard Mum and Dad arguing and shouting at each other. It made me unhappy, of course, but Martin was younger and he didn't understand what was happening. He slowly became very quiet and very angry.
Kara: On that Saturday, I was sitting in the living room with Martin while Mum and Dad were shouting at each other in the kitchen. Suddenly, I saw Martin take a box of matches from the shelf.
Kara: He lit one of the matches and moved towards the wastepaper basket. He carefully lit the paper and cardboard that was in the basket and watched the flames rise. The smell of burning was strong and Mum and Dad came running in quickly. They just stood there. I remember the look of shock in Dad's eyes. Martin started crying and I started shouting at them, telling them to stop arguing.
Kara: They spent the rest of the evening being nice to us, telling us how much they loved us. Martin liked Mum and Dad being nice to him so, a few days later, he started burning some clothes in my bedroom.
Kara: I suppose he thought that he could stop them from separating. He thought that if he kept lighting fires, they would realize how bad he felt and maybe they would stay together. But they didn't.
Kara: A few days after Dad had gone, I came home and found Martin in his room playing with cigarette lighters. I started shouting at Martin and I told him that he had to stop. I told him that Dad was never going to come home again.
Martin: You're lying! It's all your fault Mum and Dad argued.
Kara: Stop it, Martin!
Martin: It's your fault that Dad left home!
Kara: Martin, I wish you were dead!
Kara: Martin stared at me and I'll never forget the look in his eyes. He looked as if he hated me. Then he walked out of the room. I heard him leave the house, shutting the front door hard behind him. A few minutes later I went to find him.
Kara: Martin? Martin?!
Kara: I walked to the end of the street but I couldn't see him. I walked across the park near our house but he wasn't there. I looked everywhere but I couldn't find him. I sat down on a bench and felt terrible.
Kara: That was when I heard the sirens and saw two ... maybe three fire engines driving past very fast. I knew immediately that something had happened and that Martin was responsible. So I ran after the fire engines and saw them disappear round the corner into our street.
Kara: When I got to our street, there were people everywhere. The fire engines were in the middle of the street and the firefighters were breaking down the front door to our house, trying to get inside the burning building. Our home was on fire and there was nothing they could do to stop it. Forty minutes later, the house was just four walls with an empty black hole inside.

title: Episode 12: Kara's Story (Part 2)
text:
Kara: So ... That was the famous 'incident'. It was in all the newspapers and on TV. You probably saw it. I can still see the newspaper headlines – 'Pyro Boy Burns Down Broken Home'. I had to look the word up in the dictionary. 'Pyromaniac – someone who wants to start fires because they have a mental illness'. It's an ugly word. An ugly word to describe people who do terrible things.
John: And what happened to Martin? Did the police find him?
Kara: I was the one who the police interviewed. I was the one who had to see all the doctors and listen to all their questions. Nobody talked to Martin.
John: Why not?
Kara: Because ...
John: Because what? Let him go, Kara. Let him go.
Kara: What do you mean?
John: You heard his voice. You heard it when you arrived at Owl Hall, remember?
John: Stop pretending.
Kara: I'm not pretending.
John: Then tell me what really happened to Martin.
Kara: Martin is dead.
John: How did he die?
Kara: When we argued, I heard the front door shut. I thought he'd left the house. But he hadn't. He stayed in the house and started the fire. But this time I wasn't there to put it out. He died in the fire. Martin's dead.
John: So, why have you been pretending that he's still alive?
Kara: Everybody thinks it was my fault.
John: No they don't. Martin started the fire, not you. Everybody knows that.
Kara: How do you know? How do you know what everybody thinks?
John: I ...
Kara: You knew, didn't you? All this time you knew that Martin was dead! Why didn't you say anything?
John: I wanted to help you.
Kara: You work for Howard. That's why you became my friend. You're not really my friend, are you? This was all a trick!
John: No, Kara.
Kara: Leave me alone!
Mum: Kara! Where have you been? We've been looking for you everywhere. Oh darling, are you alright?
Kara: Stop lying to me! Everybody's lying to me. Tell me the truth. I want to know the truth!

title: Episode 13: A New Beginning
text:
Howard: Kara. Your mother contacted me because she thought I might be able to help you.
Mum: One of your other doctors told me about Owl Hall, Kara. It has a fantastic reputation.
Kara: A reputation for what?
Howard: Owl Hall is one of the best CTTs in the country.
Kara: CTT?
Howard: Centre for Troubled Teenagers. We provide a space for families to sort out difficulties. Being at Owl Hall is like being on holiday so we can watch the relationships between parents and children. Then we suggest ways of improving things. We also encourage our guests to write a blog so we can understand what they are thinking.
Kara: You've read my blog?
Howard: As your doctor, yes. I can promise you that everything is private. No one else has read your blog, not even your mother.
Kara: You're not my doctor.
Mum: Don't be angry, darling. You needed help. We both needed help.
Kara: It wasn't my fault. Martin's death ... the fire ...
Mum: Shush, shush, of course it wasn't your fault. It was my fault and your father's fault but it was never your fault. All this time I thought you were trying to keep Martin alive as a way to punish me. Howard has helped me understand what was really happening. I didn't know that you felt guilty too.
Howard: The main thing is that you're both getting better now, Kara – you and your mother.
Mum: Yes. Thanks to you, Howard.
Kara: Why are you thanking Howard? He didn't do anything. You should thank John.
Mum: Who's John?
Kara: He's Howard's assistant.
Mum: You never told me about an assistant.
Howard: I don't have an assistant.
Kara: Then who is John? Is he another patient?
Howard: I'm sorry, but I can't discuss other patients at Owl Hall.
Kara: John!! I need to see you!
John: Kara!
Kara: I knew you would be on your island.
John: So, we're still friends?
Kara: Yes. We're still friends.
John: Do you ever want to be someone else?
Kara: I don't know. Sometimes, I guess.
John: I do. All the time.
Kara: Why? I don't want you to be anyone else. I think you're really clever. You know more about me than I do. And you knew about this place.
John: The island?
Kara: No. Owl Hall, stupid.
John: You don't need to be clever to know what's going on here. How many holiday homes do you know with so many cameras? I knew there was something wrong with this place as soon as I arrived.
Kara: You should be a spy.
John: I know. It didn't take me long to find the basement and the key to get inside. I spent a lot of time in there, reading Howard's case files that he keeps in there. And no one ever found me. I could always see when Howard was coming back by looking at the monitors.
Kara: That's how you knew so much about my past and Martin. You read my case file.
John: And I managed to hack into the computer system so I could send you messages. Howard never discovered them.
Kara: Mum and I are leaving tomorrow.
John: I know.
Kara: But I don't want to talk about sad things now.
John: Me neither.
Kara: What was that?
John: What?
Kara: I thought I heard something. It must have been my imagination.
Ghostly voice: Kara. I'm sorry. Thanks for letting me go. I'm free now.
